triples.subject: IntraclusterStellarDensityProfile
triples.context: Individual simulation studies have shown that the intracluster stellar density profile is steeper and more centrally concentrated than the DM profile, such that the ratio 𝜌 ★/𝜌DM follows an approximate power law (e.g. Alonso Asensio et al. 2020; Reina-Campos et al. 2023; Contreras-Santos et al. 2024; Butler et al. 2025; Jeon et al. 2025), with similar trends seen observationally (e.g. Diego et al. 2023).

triples.subject: Model
triples.context: Despite the simplifying assumptions of our model, including a static, spherically symmetric halo potential and idealised satellite structure, the predicted stellar–to–DM density ratio profiles reproduce the simulation results to within < 0.2 dex over 2 orders of magnitude in radius, once differences in star-formation efficiency and central galaxy structure are accounted for.

triples.subject: InfallingSatellitePopulation
triples.context: This suggests that the properties of the infalling satellite population alone are sufficient to capture the dominant features of the ICL spatial distribution.

triples.subject: Satellite
triples.context: A central result is that the separation between the phase-space distributions of stripped stars and stripped DM is driven primarily by satellites with the most similar satellite–to–host mass ratios.

triples.subject: Satellite
